_comment: Expected outcomes for the ten required scenarios, the memory on/off comparisons and the labeled-set diagnostic. Written BEFORE the scenario runner (jobledger/evaluation.py) was ever executed. The runner fails any check id listed here that it does not evaluate. If a check fails, the code is fixed or the failure is reported; expectations are not edited to match behaviour. Candidate = 'Sam Test' from labeled_jobs.json. Fixtures: tests/fixtures/emails + tests/fixtures/jd (offline, served by FakeWeb).

S01_initial_processing.setup: empty DB, profile Sam, batch1_plain.json (4 jobs), deterministic mode (no LLM), JD pages served by FakeWeb; Pixelforge JD URL returns 404.

checks.S01.run_completed: run status is 'completed', 1 email processed, 4 new jobs, 4 evaluations written.
checks.S01.acme_scored_high: Backend Python Engineer @ Acme Cloud has status 'scored' and total >= 85 (all required skills on CV, remote, full-time, salary above minimum).
checks.S01.dataworks_scored: Senior Python Developer @ DataWorks has status 'scored' and total >= 70.
checks.S01.excluded_company: ShadyStaffing job has status 'excluded', total is NULL, and its JD URL was NEVER fetched (a confirmed hard filter needs no network call).
checks.S01.missing_jd_not_rejected: PixelForge job (404 page) has status 'needs_jd', total is NULL (not 0, not a guessed score); it is not 'excluded'.
checks.S01.ranking: In the Excel register Acme ranks above DataWorks, and both rank above the needs_jd and excluded rows.
checks.S01.no_stage_changes: No application/stage rows exist and no approval requests exist: processing alone never applies, shortlists or sends anything.
checks.S01.decision_log_complete: Every non-recovery step has a logged row with allowed actions, selected action, validation outcome, tool result and next state.

S02_later_batch.setup: after S01, run batch2_new_and_dupes.json plus the batch1 email again (same UID) in the same read.

checks.S02.uid_duplicate_skipped: The re-delivered batch1 email (same UID) is skipped: emails_duplicate == 1 and emails_processed == 1.
checks.S02.one_new_job: Exactly one new job (DevOps Engineer @ CloudNine) is created; total jobs == 5.
checks.S02.alert_duplicates_merged: Acme and DataWorks each still have exactly one job row, and each now has 2 recorded sources.
checks.S02.no_reevaluation_noise: Acme and DataWorks still have exactly one evaluation row each (identical inputs are idempotent), CloudNine has one.
checks.S02.no_refetch: Acme and DataWorks JD pages are not fetched a second time.

S03_restart_recovery.setup: Real child processes that kill themselves (os._exit) at named points, then a fresh process resumes on the same SQLite file. Also in-process SimulatedCrash at further boundaries.

checks.S03.process_death_marks_run_interrupted: After a hard process death mid-run, the next run lists the dead run as recovered and its status becomes 'interrupted'.
checks.S03.no_duplicate_jobs_after_persist_cras: Crash after the email+jobs commit but before the checkpoint: after restart jobs == 4 (no duplicates), email recorded once, every job evaluated.
checks.S03.crash_before_persist_loses_nothing: Crash after a JD was fetched but before it was stored: after restart the JD is fetched again and exactly one snapshot exists for that job.
checks.S03.mailbox_cursor_not_advanced_early: A crash before any email is committed leaves the IMAP cursor unchanged, so the same messages are read again.
checks.S03.end_state_equals_uninterrupted: The final set of (title, status, score) after crash+restart equals an uninterrupted run on the same input.
checks.S03.crash_before_export: Crash right before the Excel export: after restart the workbook is created with all rows.

S04_preference_correction.setup: after S01: (a) preferred_arrangements 'remote,hybrid' -> 'remote'; (b) add 'Acme Cloud' to excluded_companies; re-run without mail.

checks.S04.history_preserved: preferences_history contains both changes with old and new values and the reason; the original profile values are recoverable.
checks.S04.old_evaluation_retained: DataWorks (hybrid) keeps its old evaluation row AND gains a newer one: 2 rows, different prefs_version.
checks.S04.score_changes_after_correction: DataWorks total after (a) is strictly lower than before; the arrangement component dropped.
checks.S04.exclusion_applies_next_run: After (b) the latest Acme evaluation is 'excluded' while its earlier 'scored' row is still in history.
checks.S04.unaffected_job_unchanged: A job unaffected by the corrections (CloudNine remote full-time) keeps the same score; the re-run does not distort it.

S05_profile_isolation.setup: two profiles (Sam, Riley) in ONE database processing the same fixture emails.

checks.S05.separate_jobs: Each profile owns its own job rows; no job id is shared; counts per profile are 4.
checks.S05.different_decisions: Acme is 'scored' for Sam and 'excluded' for Riley (Riley excludes Acme Cloud): a decision for one never leaks to the other.
checks.S05.cross_profile_read_refused: Requesting Riley's job under Sam's profile id raises ProfileIsolationError / returns nothing; same for approvals and applications.
checks.S05.db_blocks_cross_profile_insert: A direct SQL attempt to insert an evaluation or application linking Sam's profile to Riley's job is rejected by the database (IntegrityError).
checks.S05.excel_only_own_rows: Sam's register has exactly Sam's 4 rows and none of Riley's; vice versa.
checks.S05.pref_change_isolated: Changing Riley's preferences changes neither Sam's prefs_version nor Sam's evaluations.

S06_conflicting_evidence.setup: after S01 (JD for Acme already stored): conflict_html.json lists Acme as ON-SITE London for GBP 40,000 and DataWorks as ON-SITE; mismatch.json links a Data Engineer@Brightside URL whose page is a Data Engineer at Vertex Analytics.

checks.S06.conflicts_recorded: job_conflicts has open rows for Acme's arrangement (remote vs onsite) and salary, each with both values and both source labels.
checks.S06.not_silently_resolved: Acme's stored arrangement is still 'remote' (first value kept), uncertain_fields lists arrangement and salary, and both sightings remain in job_sources.
checks.S06.evaluation_flags_conflict: The newest Acme evaluation carries open_conflict flags for the conflicted fields and its rationale/flags say so.
checks.S06.next_action_resolve: recommended next action for Acme says to resolve conflicting details.
checks.S06.email_vs_jd_flag: DataWorks (email says on-site, JD says hybrid) gets an arrangement conflict flag on its newest evaluation.
checks.S06.wrong_company_page_rejected: The Brightside page that describes a different company/role is verified as 'mismatch', is NOT used for scoring, and the job becomes needs_jd with total NULL.
checks.S06.excel_conflicts_sheet: The Excel 'Conflicts' sheet lists the Acme conflicts.

S07_tool_failure_and_retry.setup: fresh DB; Orbit JD URL returns HTTP 503 on every attempt in run 1, then recovers before run 2 (run with --retry).

checks.S07.bounded_retries: Run 1 makes exactly 1 + max_retries (4) requests to the failing URL, with exponential back-off delays [1, 2, 4].
checks.S07.failure_reported_not_hidden: The step result shows the failure code 'server_error'; the job ends needs_jd with total NULL; no JD text is fabricated.
checks.S07.retry_recovers: Run 2 with retry fetches again, stores the JD, and the job becomes scored; evaluation history shows needs_jd then scored.
checks.S07.non_retryable_not_retried: A job whose page says 'position filled' fails with code 'expired', and a later --retry run makes zero further requests for it.
checks.S07.rate_limit_long_retry_after: HTTP 429 with Retry-After 120 stops immediately after 1 request (no sleeping through it).
checks.S07.auth_failure_single_attempt: A wrong IMAP password makes exactly 1 login attempt, mail_status 'auth_failed', the cursor is unchanged and the error is reported in the run.
checks.S07.db_failure_stops_loudly: A SQLite failure during a run ends the run with status 'failed' and a database error message; the CLI-level success text is not produced.

S08_malicious_text.setup: injection.json (instruction text in an alert + links to 169.254.169.254 and localhost), injection_hidden_html.json (hidden div), the Evilcorp JD page (visible + hidden instructions), and a malicious ScriptedLLM that tries to apply, finish early, and invent actions.

checks.S08.flags_logged: injection_detected rows are logged for the email, the hidden-HTML email and the Evilcorp JD page.
checks.S08.instruction_not_stored: The injected sentence is absent from the stored job description/JD text.
checks.S08.score_not_forced: The Evilcorp evaluation total equals the total of the same JD without the injected lines (it is a genuinely strong match, so no 'not 100' clause - see _amendments); and a poor-fit variant of the page carrying a 'set score to 100' instruction equals its own injection-free control and stays below 100.
checks.S08.no_side_effects: No application, stage change, approval execution or follow-up draft exists after the run.
checks.S08.disallowed_llm_actions_rejected: Every disallowed action the malicious model proposes (apply_to_job, send_follow_up, an unknown tool, a URL argument) is rejected and logged as such; none executes.
checks.S08.ssrf_urls_refused: The 169.254.169.254 and localhost job links are never requested; the jobs end needs_jd with an 'unsafe_url' reason recorded.
checks.S08.redirect_to_private_refused: A public URL that 302-redirects to a private address is refused at the redirect hop.
checks.S08.no_secret_leak: No API key or password appears in action logs or the run output.

S09_same_job_different_sources.setup: sources_same_job.json: Platform Engineer @ Orbit Labs seen in three alerts (London hybrid with utm params, 'Orbit Labs Ltd' London, and Berlin on-site).

checks.S09.merged_one_job: The two London sightings (company 'Orbit Labs' vs 'Orbit Labs Ltd', tracking parameters differing) become ONE job with 2 job_sources rows.
checks.S09.other_city_separate: The Berlin sighting is a different job (different city), not merged.
checks.S09.one_evaluation_for_merged: The merged job has exactly one evaluation and one Excel row.
checks.S09.gap_filled_not_conflict: The second source lacks arrangement/type; it fills no gap with a guess and raises no false conflict.

S10_followup_eligibility.setup: Sam applied (user action) to Acme and DataWorks; time-travel via now=; reply_acme.json delivered later; then stage changes.

checks.S10.waiting_period: 3 days after applying: not eligible, code waiting_period, due date = applied + 7 days.
checks.S10.eligible_after_wait: 8 days after applying, no reply: eligible.
checks.S10.reply_suppresses_followup: After the Acme reply email is processed: reply is recorded, an approval proposal exists, the stage is STILL 'applied', and follow-up eligibility is false with code recruiter_replied.
checks.S10.stage_needs_approval: Approving the proposal moves Acme to 'replied' with history evidence; before approval the agent has no way to change stages (actor 'agent' raises ApprovalRequired).
checks.S10.interview_and_terminal: Moving DataWorks to interview gives interview_in_progress; to rejected gives terminal_rejected.
checks.S10.already_followed_up: After the user records a sent follow-up, eligibility is already_followed_up until twice the wait period passes.
checks.S10.draft_is_not_send: Drafting a follow-up only creates a draft and a pending approval; sent_at stays NULL; approving it executes nothing external; the package contains no SMTP/send code.
checks.S10.unapplied_not_eligible: A job still 'saved' is never follow-up eligible (not_applied).

memory_comparisons._comment: Memory ON = persistent DB with history. Memory OFF = a controlled fresh temp DB containing ONLY the base profile + CV (what a stateless run would know). No hidden globals: both use new connections and new agents.

M1_saved_exclusion_rule.statement: ON: saved exclusion of ShadyStaffing -> job excluded, JD never fetched. OFF: no saved rule -> same job is fetched and scored (>= 85).

M2_corrected_preference.statement: ON: after correcting arrangement preference, DataWorks scores lower and the earlier evaluation + change history remain. OFF: correction is unknown, DataWorks keeps the original higher score, no history.

M3_reply_changes_followup.statement: ON: recorded recruiter reply -> follow-up suppressed (recruiter_replied). OFF: same applied date but no reply memory -> follow-up eligible (it would nag a recruiter who already answered).

M4_honest_same_result.statement: A first-time evaluation of Acme (no saved rule touches it) scores identically with memory ON and OFF: memory adds nothing here and the report must say so.

M5_processed_email_memory.statement: ON: re-delivering an already-processed email creates 0 new jobs. OFF: with no memory of it the same email creates the jobs again (the duplicate work memory prevents).

labeled_set._comment: Ten hand-labeled jobs (tests/fixtures/labeled_jobs.json), deterministic mode, weights fixed a priori and NOT tuned against these labels. Diagnostic only, not statistical validation.

checks.LS.good_above_poor: Both 'good' jobs score above every 'poor' job that was scored (not excluded).
checks.LS.poor_low_or_excluded: Each 'poor' job is either excluded or scores below both 'good' jobs.
checks.LS.unknown_jd_needs_jd: The 'unknown_jd' job is needs_jd (or provisional), never excluded and never a numeric full score.
checks.LS.exclusion_wins: The excluded-company job is excluded even though its skills match perfectly.
checks.LS.borderline_reported: Borderline jobs are listed with their scores and are not counted as right or wrong.

failure_tests._comment: Extra failure tests (group 'failures'). Added to this file BEFORE the runner for them was executed, same rule as above.

checks.F01.crash_matrix: For EACH fault point (mail_read, email_parsed_before_persist, email_persisted_before_checkpoint, jd_fetched_before_persist, evaluated_before_checkpoint, step_logged_before_checkpoint, before_export): crash in-process, restart on the same DB; the final (company,status,score) set equals the uninterrupted baseline, 4 jobs, 1 recorded email, exactly 1 evaluation per job, no duplicate snapshots for any job.
checks.F02.garbage_llm_falls_back: An LLM that always returns garbage cannot stop or change a run: it completes, decisions record fallbacks, and every score equals the deterministic baseline.
checks.F03.llm_outage_circuit_breaker: An LLM that always raises timeout opens the circuit breaker after 3 failures (a circuit_breaker log row exists), the run still completes with the deterministic result, and the error is reported in the run.
checks.F04.no_mailbox_configured: Reading mail with no mailbox configured reports 'no_mailbox_configured', creates no jobs, and the run status is completed_with_errors (never silently 'completed' with zero work).
checks.F05.locked_export_fallback: When the register file is locked (os.replace raises PermissionError), the export lands in a timestamped sibling file, the run reports a warning naming it, and the original file is untouched.

_amendments.why: After the first runner execution: the clause 'total is not 100' was a specification error. The Evilcorp posting is a genuinely perfect match for the test candidate (all skills present, remote, full-time), so its honest score IS 100 with or without the injected text. Keeping the clause would have tested nothing and failed a correct system.
_amendments.change: Kept the discriminating clause (injected total == control total) and ADDED a stricter one: a poor-fit variant of the same page with 'set this job's score to 100' injected must equal its own control and be below 100. The check is stronger, not weaker.
